name: Street Custom 'Ghost' Printed Pistol
description:
A 3D-printed single-shot pistol manufactured on consumer-grade fabrication equipment using freely available design files. The Ghost is produced from high-temperature polymer with a printed barrel, frame, and firing mechanism — the only non-printed component is a short steel barrel liner pressed into the polymer bore and a hardware-store nail for the firing pin. The weapon fires a single 9mm round with enough accuracy and reliability to function as a lethal tool at ranges under 5 meters.

Ghost pistols exist because fabrication technology has made weapons manufacturing a file-sharing problem. The design files circulate on encrypted networks, updated regularly by anonymous engineers who refine the geometry based on field reports and failure analysis. Version 14 — the current standard — has a reliable firing rate of approximately 90% and a barrel life of 8-12 rounds before the steel liner shifts in the polymer housing and accuracy becomes dangerously unpredictable.

The Ghost's most dangerous characteristic is its near-invisibility to standard screening. The polymer frame contains no metal except the barrel liner and firing pin — two small pieces that can be disguised as belt buckle components or hair accessories during separate passage through screening. The weapon can be assembled in 30 seconds from seemingly innocuous parts, fired, and discarded. A Ghost pistol that has been used in a crime looks identical to random polymer debris in a waste container. It is a weapon designed to exist for exactly as long as it is needed and then cease to exist.
legality: Illegal — unregistered firearm; manufacturing constitutes weapons production
street_price: Φ15-50 (printing cost plus nail and liner)
specifications:
caliber: 9mm
capacity: 1 round
effective range: 5 meters
barrel life: 8-12 rounds
weight: 150g
length: 180mm
material: High-temperature polymer with steel barrel liner
firing reliability: ~90% (Version 14)
tactical_use: Disposable close-range weapon for single-use operations. The Ghost is printed, assembled, used, and discarded. Its value is not in its capability — which is minimal — but in its untraceability and its ability to pass security screening in component form.
cultural_context: The Ghost represents the democratization of weapons manufacturing — anyone with a consumer fabricator can produce a lethal weapon from a downloaded file. This has created a constant arms race between screening technology and printing innovation, with each new detection method met by a new design that evades it. The Ghost's name is apt: it appears, kills, and vanishes.
known_users: Individuals planning operations in screened environments
Political assassins requiring disposable untraceable weapons
story_hooks: A new Ghost design file has appeared that prints a multi-shot mechanism — three rounds instead of one, with a rotating barrel assembly. The file's metadata contains a message: 'Version 15. They can't stop us from making what we need.'

A high-security corporate facility has experienced three killings with Ghost pistols in two months. The weapons were assembled inside the facility using a fabricator in the employee workshop. The design file was found on 40% of employee personal devices.

physical_description.visual_profile: A crude, almost organic-looking single-shot pistol with an angular, minimalist silhouette. The frame appears skeletal and deliberately stripped down, lacking any traditional gunsmith refinement. It looks like something halfway between a tool prototype and a toy — unnervingly simple and deliberately disposable.
physical_description.dimensions: 180mm length, 95mm height (grip to rear sight plane), 25mm width across grip. Barrel liner approximately 60mm protruding from front of frame.
physical_description.weight_description: Surprisingly light and fragile-feeling in hand — 150g makes it feel almost hollow. No heft or reassuring weight. Imbalance toward the barrel despite the short length.
physical_description.primary_material: High-temperature polymer (likely PEEK or polycarbonate blend) with a pressed steel barrel liner and single steel nail firing pin.
physical_description.finish: Matte off-white to light gray with visible layer lines from the 3D printing process. The polymer has a slight translucency in bright light, revealing hollow voids and internal geometry meant to be invisible. No coating, no polish — just raw print finish with minor surface irregularities and occasional under-extrusion marks.
physical_description.color_scheme: Predominant pale gray-white polymer with dull steel barrel liner visible at the muzzle. Minor discoloration from post-print handling.
physical_description.grip_texture: Bare polymer with subtle horizontal ridges from print layers. Slightly textured from rapid cooling, not ergonomic — uncomfortable to hold for extended periods. No tape, no grip enhancement.
distinctive_features: Visible print layer lines across entire frame surface
Minimal sighting plane — crude molded notch at rear, front sight barely raised
Single fire hole in the frame with no trigger guard — just an open lever made of printed polymer
Exposed barrel liner showing concentric tool marks from pressing process
Hollow interior visible through semi-translucent polymer sections
No slide, no moving parts except the nail-pin striker mechanism
Intentionally featureless — no brand markings, serial numbers, or identifying information
Hairline stress fractures visible in polymer grip where rough assembly forces were applied
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: None. The Ghost is unmarked by design. Some versions show a barely-visible file hash etched in 2mm text on the interior of the grip — meaningless to anyone without the encryption key, but present as version identification for the underground network.
physical_description.condition_typical: Appears freshly printed but deliberately neglected. Surface shows light handling marks and dust accumulation. The weapon exists in a state of controlled decay — functional but visibly temporary. No maintenance, no cleaning, no care. It looks like it was meant to be thrown away.

image_prompt: Overhead flat-lay product shot of a disassembled Street Custom Ghost pistol on brushed dark titanium surface. Main components separated: pale gray 3D-printed polymer frame with visible layer lines and stress marks, short dark steel barrel liner, single exposed steel nail firing pin. Dramatic side-lighting at 45 degrees casting sharp shadows, emphasizing the crude geometry and hollow interior visible through translucent polymer sections. Cyberpunk aesthetic with minimalist composition — no branding, no flourish, just clinical documentation of a disposable weapon. Cool color grading with slight cyan-blue tint on metal components.
